claim: Exponential growth: one RK4 step multiplies the cells by R(z) with z = r·Δt, N steps by R(z)^N, and N steps fall short of the exact x₀·e^(rt) by at most N·e^((N−1)z)·(z⁵/120)/(1 − z/6) of x₀.
derivation: dx/dt = r·x with r = 0.3 per day, Δt = 0.25 day and x₀ = 50 cells: f is linear with λ = r, so z = λ·Δt = 0.075 (MODEL.md E3).
So x after n steps is 50·R(z)^n: 53.89420654296875 after 1 step and 1004.2760998493397 after 40 (t = 10 days), computed with exact fractions and rounded once.

Rounding: about ten roundings a step, each within 1.1e-16 of a value below 1005, so within about 1e-12 after one step (tolerance 1e-10) and 4.4e-11 after 40 (tolerance 1e-9). r = 0.3 is not exact in binary, but its error, 1.1e-17, moves x after 10 days by about 10 × 1.1e-17 of itself, 1.1e-13.
The exact solution at t = 10 days is 50·e³ = 1004.2768461593834.
e^z − R(z) = Σ over m ≥ 5 of z^m/m!, every term positive, each at most z/6 of the one before, so 0 < e^z − R(z) ≤ (z⁵/120)/(1 − z/6) = 2.00257e-8.
Calculator check with exact fractions: 50e³ − 50R⁴⁰ = 7.4631e-4, inside the bound and just under it, as it should be: e^(jz)R^(N−1−j) is close to e^((N−1)z) when R is close to e^z.

anchors.need: None: a hand-built oracle model, taken from no paper.
